subject: SentinelBridge — evidence access matrix & handoff
messages:
From: Anya Kozlov <anya@sentinelbridge.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: devops@sentinelbridge.com, security@sentinelbridge.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence access matrix + automated handoff options

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. SentinelBridge is ready to start the evidence-handoff integration for SOC 2 / pen-test artifacts. To help scope the work, I attached our initial evidence access matrix (sentinelbridge_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx) — it lists evidence types, retention needs, and preferred access methods (SFTP pull, pre-signed S3, or API).

Quick asks:
- Can Redwood support an SFTP pull endpoint scoped to a partner identity (we can rotate keys)?
- If SSO is required, do you accept SCIM provisioning + a service account?
- Any minimum encryption/cipher requirements for in-transit and at-rest?

We'd like to automate delivery for recurring reports and to get a brief runbook for manual escalations (who to contact, ticketing). Also attaching a small template for SFTP credentials we typically exchange so you can see the fields we expect (sftp_credentials_template.txt).

If helpful I can schedule a 30-min sync with our DevOps and security leads — proposed times Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Best,
Anya Kozlov
Partnerships & Integrations
SentinelBridge

Attachments: sentinelbridge_evidence_matrix_v1.xlsx, sftp_credentials_template.txt

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Anya Kozlov <anya@sentinelbridge.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 14:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence access matrix + automated handoff options

Anya —

Thanks for the matrix and the templates — very helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we book a sync:

- SFTP pull: we can run a scheduled job that pulls from partner SFTP, but for security/compliance we prefer inbound push (pre-signed S3 or HTTPS POST with client cert). That said, we can support SFTP pull if you prefer; we'll need an ACL matrix and rotation cadence.
- SCIM/SSO: Redwood supports SCIM for provisioning and OIDC for service accounts. For automation, a SCIM service object with a dedicated role is ideal.
- Encryption: we require TLS 1.2+ for in-transit and AES-256 for at-rest by default; if you have alternative cipher constraints share them and we'll validate.

Action items I propose:
1) Quick technical sync (30m) to align on preferred transfer method and sample files.
2) We (Redwood) will draft a minimal MOU for evidence handling and retention to attach to our SOC 2 appendix.
3) Security will run a short checklist against the matrix and flag any items that need additional controls.

I'm looping in Stephanie (security/compliance) and Marcus (platform integrations) — they can speak to SFTP job ops and our retention SLA. 

Proposed times: Wed 06/16 9:00-9:30 PT or Thu 06/17 11:00-11:30 PT. Which works?

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0198

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Anya Kozlov <anya@sentinelbridge.com>, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence access matrix + automated handoff options

Hi Anya —

Quick note from security:
- We reviewed the matrix and there are three item classes we treat as elevated: pen-test raw logs, ephemeral debug artifacts, and customer PII exports. For those we require atomic delivery (no partial pulls) and immutable checks (checksums).
- For automated ingestion we prefer pre-signed S3 PUTs to our ingestion bucket with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). If you cannot do PUTs, HTTPS POST with client certs is acceptable.
- We will not accept partner-initiated long-lived SFTP keys; keys must be rotated every 30 days and audited.

I drafted a short MOU and added it to the Drive folder — see the doc named mou-sentinelbridge-redwood-20260617.pdf. The MOU includes contact points for incident escalation and an initial retention schedule.

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Anya Kozlov <anya@sentinelbridge.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: devops@sentinelbridge.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence access matrix + automated handoff options

Thanks Stephanie & Tessa —

All good notes. We can do pre-signed S3 PUTs with SSE-KMS. DevOps confirmed they will build a small publisher that:
- Generates pre-signed PUT URLs per artifact
- Attaches SHA256 checksum metadata
- Rotates the publisher API key every 14 days

We reviewed your MOU and made two small redlines (non-substantive): update contact email for security@sentinelbridge.com and confirm retention for pen-test raw logs is 180 days on our side. Also attaching the signed MOU from our legal team (mou-sentinelbridge-redwood-20260617.pdf).

We're good to run a smoke test week of Jun 21. If that works for Redwood, we'll schedule a 30m window on Mon 06/21.

— Anya

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Anya Kozlov <anya@sentinelbridge.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence access matrix + automated handoff options

Anya —

Mon 06/21 10:00 AM PT works for the smoke test. Marcus will coordinate the ingestion side; Stephanie will run verification of checksums and retention slots after the test.

Quick checklist for the smoke test:
- One pen-test artifact (zip), one compliance report (pdf), and one system log (ndjson).
- Pre-signed PUT URLs valid for 30 minutes.
- SHA256 metadata header and file checksum in the manifest.

Marcus — can you add the ingestion job to our barnyard queue and confirm a warm worker will be available?

Thanks team — looking forward to getting this into automation. I'll upload the signed MOU to our partner Drive folder after the call and link the Jira ticket SEC-421.

Best,
Tessa
Partnerships Lead, Redwood Inference
